wa_liberty_bell_nw_face.notes: A left-trending gully/crack system past a couple of trees; the low-angle crack feels harder than its grade if you avoid stemming off the mid-pitch tree.
A crack system left of a 2-3 ft chimney, with a piton near the top; pull over a 4-5 ft horn before easier 4th-class scrambling.

A left-facing corner of large, thin flakes -- three crack systems are visible; stay right on the good flake and avoid the middle splitter (the harder 5.10d Remsberg Variation). Loose rock underfoot makes this a mental, PG13 crux.

The 'money pitch': a shaded, north-facing dihedral with a thin, cruxy lower section of laybacks, finger jams and fancy footwork, easing into a blank, runout corner (20-30 ft) near the top. The pitch runs long -- expect to stretch a 60m rope.
Easy terrain up and left gains Liberty Bell's west summit, from which a short scramble reaches the true (main) summit.

wa_liberty_bell_sidewinder.notes: Three starts are possible: a 5th-class traverse in from the left onto the main shelf, a ramp past a tree, or broken ground below a cave. They meet at an awkward, slabby mantel with the last piece below your feet, then a short runout reaches the base of the crack and a small belay stance.

Climb the widening hand crack. Either belay at a slung chockstone, or continue about 35 ft higher to a large alcove that has good cracks for an anchor. The choice decides which P3 variation is convenient.

Two options to the same spacious ledge. 3a takes a clean, wider crack in a flaring feature, then easy face climbing right and back left to lower-angled ground below a bulge. 3b steps about 10 ft right from the alcove to a thin finger crack; the moves where that crack runs out are the spiciest on the route, before easy face to the ledge.
Go up the bulge on a crack; the ground eases steadily above it and several lines are possible. Several cracks go; any of them leads to the easier ground above.
Mostly 4th-class scrambling toward the summit. Many parties move together here; watch for others on the Beckey Route converging on the same ground.

wa_mount_thomson_west_ridge.notes: An exposed step out over the gully on the left, then a right-trending chimney feature up to trees; one easy 5.6 move off the ground, then low 5th to the tree belay.
An exposed rightward ramp, then back left toward unlikely-looking roofs described as the route's physical crux; belay on a ledge just above.
A short wall (watch for a stuck cam at the top) leads through dirty tree ledges and steps to a belay at the base of a hanging slab.
Float up the slab, over a bush/tree, then right and up through steeper, exposed moves with an interesting layback midway.
The last technical climbing before the party coils the rope for the scramble across the false summit to the true summit.
